newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Norsk Hydro rises on results.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Norsk Hydro rises on results.

text.p: Norwegian industrial conglomerate Norsk Hydro A/S rose on Monday, boosted by first quarter earnings to highlight trade in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Traders said ADRs were bolstered by a weakening dollar, adding that the market was rather quiet because no major economic data was expected this week.
"We think this could be sort of a non-eventful week since the market has had a big move" last week, a trader said. "We could see lateral movements this week -- the focus is on the dollar."

Norsk Hydro rose 2-7/8 to 48-3/4 in light volume after it reported first quarter earnings per share of 6.70 crowns against 8.20 for the same period last year. The earnings were better than analysts expected.
ADRs in British software developer Planning Sciences International Plc fell 1-3/8 to 3-3/8, a 12-month low. Volume was 886,300 shares and the ADRs were among the loss leaders on the Nasdaq exchange.
The company said last week it expected a small profit for the first quarter. After the announcement, Alex. Brown cut its rating for Planning Sciences to market performer from buy.
The ADRs have fallen from a high of about 32 in May 1996.
Among oil stocks, Royal Dutch Petroleum was up 1-5/8 at 177-1/8 and British Petroleum Co Plc rose 1-7/8 to 135-1/2. French oil company Elf Aquitaine fell 1-1/8 to 46-3/4.
Among Latin American ADRs, Brazilian telephone company Telebras SA rose one to 110-7/8.
Advancers led decliners 211 to 204 among 806 ADRs. The ADR index was up 0.04 and volume in late morning was 23 million shares.
